newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Forex intervention wanes in major currencies - BIS.
newsitem.headline: Forex intervention wanes in major currencies - BIS.

text.p: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) said German and U.S. monetary authorities engaged in no intervention in the foreign exchange markets in 1996, or in first quarter of 1997.
The Bank of Japan also was inactive in the past year.

"The Bank of Japan, after showing a $21 billion increase in reserves in the first quarter of 1996 from intervention and interest receipts, does not seem to have intervened in the next 12 months," BIS said.

It said that a $14 billion increase in Japanese reserves over the last nine months of 1996 "appears to represent mainly the flow of earnings on a stock of foreign exchange reserves that reached $207 billion by the end of the year."

Its comments, in its annual report, were contained in a review of the world's foreign exchange reserves held at central banks. It said the reserves grew by a record amount of almost $200 billion in 1996 in constant terms.
In a table, the BIS said total foreign exchange reserves at constant exchange rates rose $196.5 billion to $1.518 trillion.
BIS said that most of the growth in official reserves was in other parts of Asia besides Japan, especially China, and in Latin America.

"In Europe, Spain and Italy also built up reserves substantially as foreign investors bought peseta and lira bonds and the Bank of Spain and the Bank of Italy intervened to buy dollars or marks," BIS said.
